title: Data-Driven Decision Support in SaaS Cloud-Based Service Models
authors: Charizanis, G.; Mavridou, E.; Vrochidou, E.; Kalampokas, T.; Papakostas, G.A.
tldr: A scoping review of 28 studies on data-driven decision support in SaaS, finding churn prediction as the dominant focus and Random Forest and XGBoost as top-performing algorithms.
problem_and_motivation: SaaS providers face high customer churn and intense competition, yet existing literature reviews on data-driven decision support for SaaS are fragmented, outdated, or lack systematic methodology. Prior reviews focused narrowly on churn prediction in non-SaaS industries, leaving a gap in holistic coverage of engagement, segmentation, and retention strategies. There is a need for a comprehensive, systematic survey that compares ML methods and evaluates their effectiveness across multiple SaaS decision-making contexts.
approach: Conducted a PRISMA-ScR scoping review searching Scopus and Google Scholar from 2014 to 2025.
Applied four research questions addressing focus areas, data sources, ML effectiveness, and output forms.
Screened 426 initial results down to 28 papers through two-phase relevance filtering.
Categorized reviewed papers by decision support objective including churn prediction, segmentation, CLV, and engagement.
Compared ML algorithm performance across studies using AUC, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics.
Analyzed output types: visualizations, simulation tools, segmentation, business metrics, and deployment strategies.
Synthesized strategic recommendations for ML model selection based on use case and data characteristics.
findings: 53.57% of reviewed papers focused on churn prediction as the dominant decision support objective.
num: Random Forest achieved up to 98.8% accuracy and 0.997 AUC in churn prediction studies.
num: XGBoost achieved 98.8% AUC in mobile freemium game churn prediction.
num: Hybrid SVM-Naive Bayes model achieved 95.67% accuracy and 95.65% recall in CRM churn prediction.
num: LASSO regression personalized free trial lengths, yielding 6.8% subscription increase over 30-day baseline.
num: UI design improvements linked to 41% increase in customer loyalty via PLS-SEM analysis.
num: Hybrid LSTM ensemble achieved 60% better decile lift and 25% higher AUROC than standalone BiLSTM.
num: XGBoost training produced 335% higher carbon emissions than logistic regression.
No studies employed SHAP or LIME explainability techniques for model interpretation.
Behavioral and usage data were the most common data category across all reviewed studies.

definitions.definition: Software as a Service, a cloud-based software delivery model where users access applications via subscription.
The percentage of users that cancel their subscriptions in a SaaS business.
Customer Lifetime Value, predicting the future revenue customers may generate.
Random Forest, an ensemble learning method for classification and regression.
Area Under the Curve, a metric measuring classifier performance across all thresholds.
Long Short-Term Memory, a recurrent neural network architecture for sequential data.
Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews.
Monthly Recurring Revenue, a key SaaS business metric.
Net Promoter Score, a customer satisfaction and loyalty metric.
Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection, a dimensionality reduction technique.
Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise, a clustering algorithm.
Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling, a multivariate statistical method.
SHapley Additive exPlanations, a method for explaining ML model predictions.
Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations, a technique for explaining individual predictions.
Machine Learning as a Service, cloud-based platforms providing ML model deployment and monitoring.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper provides the first comprehensive scoping review of data-driven decision support systems specifically tailored to SaaS cloud-based service models, filling a gap left by prior reviews that focused narrowly on churn prediction or non-SaaS domains. It systematically evaluates 28 studies across four research questions, benchmarking ML algorithms including Random Forest, XGBoost, LSTM, and hybrid architectures on real-world SaaS datasets. The review establishes that ensemble methods consistently outperform simpler classifiers for tabular behavioral data, while hybrid models excel at capturing temporal dynamics. It further identifies critical unaddressed research gaps around model explainability, algorithmic fairness, privacy-preserving techniques, and the environmental carbon footprint of ML model training. The work synthesizes actionable guidelines for algorithm selection based on business objective and data characteristics.
directly_justifies: Random Forest and XGBoost consistently outperform other ML models in churn prediction tasks with tabular data.
Hybrid LSTM-based architectures capture temporal dynamics better than static models for sequential user behavior.
No reviewed study employed SHAP or LIME for model explainability in SaaS decision support.
XGBoost training produced 335% higher carbon emissions than logistic regression in one study.
53.57% of reviewed papers focused on churn prediction as the primary decision support objective.
Behavioral and usage data are the most common input type across all reviewed decision support systems.
limits: Review limited to Scopus and Google Scholar databases, excluding Web of Science and other sources.
Time range restricted to 2014-2025, potentially missing earlier foundational work.
Only 28 papers met inclusion criteria, limiting the generalizability of comparative conclusions.
Most reviewed studies used proprietary datasets, reducing reproducibility.
The review does not provide its own empirical validation of the synthesized recommendations.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned against the paper's content. Domain 4 (Landscape and Limitations of Existing Systems) was flagged as highly relevant because the paper is a scoping review that maps the landscape of data-driven DSS in SaaS and explicitly identifies gaps in explainability, fairness, and privacy. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) received medium relevance because the paper benchmarks predictive ML algorithms though not in personal finance specifically. Domain 11 (Engagement Dynamics) received medium relevance due to extensive discussion of churn, retention, and user engagement. Domains 12.A and 12.B (Evaluation Frameworks and Algorithmic Evaluation) received high relevance as the paper systematically compares model performance. Domain 5.A (Financial Behavioral Profiles) received low relevance as user segmentation is discussed but in a SaaS rather than personal finance context. Domains 1-3 (Filipino demographics, cultural practices, expense categorization) were considered and rejected as the paper focuses on cloud software services, not personal budgeting. Domains 7-8 (Budgeting strategies, Anomaly detection), 9 (Mobile-first design), 10 (Privacy and trust), 13 (Savings and debt), and 14 (Synthetic data, ML deployment) were considered and rejected or assigned low contextual relevance. The paper's overall topical coverage centers on ML algorithm benchmarking for user retention and engagement in cloud software business models.

limitations: Database coverage limited to Scopus and Google Scholar, excluding Web of Science and PubMed.
Review time range restricted to 2014-2025, potentially missing earlier foundational work.
Only 28 papers met inclusion criteria from 426 initial results, limiting statistical generalizability.
Most reviewed studies used proprietary datasets, reducing reproducibility and cross-study comparability.
No empirical validation of the synthesized algorithm selection recommendations was conducted.
Gaming industry studies represent a significant portion of the sample, potentially skewing generalizability to enterprise SaaS.
remember_this: Churn prediction is the dominant objective in 53.57% of reviewed SaaS decision support studies.
Random Forest and XGBoost consistently outperform other algorithms for tabular behavioral data.
No reviewed study used SHAP or LIME explainability techniques despite their proven value.
XGBoost produces 335% higher carbon emissions than logistic regression, raising sustainability concerns.
Hybrid LSTM architectures outperform static models for capturing temporal user behavior patterns.
